Thomason is sixth of the six names in the fourth block and the crop is the sixth of the six portraits in the fourth row; the block reads Randy S. Terry, Dina S. Tharp, Dennis Cary Thomas, Linda Key Thomas, Norman Dale Thomas, Alice Rebecca Thomason, that is man, woman, man, woman, man, woman, and the fourth row of faces alternates in exactly that order. Taylor is fifth of the five names in the fourth block and the crop is the fifth of the five portraits in the fourth row; the block reads James Ronald Tabb, Martha Owens Talley, Charla Tichenor Taub, Mitchell Irwin Taub, Bobbye Taylor, that is man, woman, woman, man, woman, and the fourth row of faces matches it exactly. The eleven other Taylors indexed in the volume all carry other given names.

1972 Talisman, p. 273, the Associated Students group photograph of the women members. The caption gives ten names to the front row and thirteen to the row behind, and the photograph holds exactly that: ten women kneeling along the flower bed and thirteen standing behind them. Armuth is first of the thirteen second-row names and the crop is the figure at the left-hand end of that standing band. The reading of the row is checked against four women in it whose portraits the archive now holds: Chris Moore fourth, Nancy Manar seventh, Nancy Burdett eleventh and Robbie Coatney twelfth, together with Mary Coleman tenth, the only woman in the band with a full afro and a match for the portrait the archive already holds of her. The front row checks the same way, with Carolyn Ragland third and Cheryl Mack tenth. The volume's only other Armuth is Michael Harold, a freshman.

years.caption: The Herald's portraits of the winners as the result stood on 15 April 1999: President Amanda Coates and Vice President Cassie Martin, who took the presidency on a recount, 614-611; vice president of finance Joe Matheis; vice president of administration Brandon Griffey; and vice president of public relations Matt Bastin. Matheis never took office — the Judicial Council voided the finance race on 20 April over election code violations, and Ryan Morrison won the re-run and served the year.
